_comment: Phrases that must NOT appear anywhere in the wiki. qa_wiki.py --ban turns every
This is the single most valuable QA artefact in the kit, and the reason is
specific: in the reference run the subject's own README claimed 'syntax
highlighting' and 'nested lists'. Neither existed. Both claims were plausible,
both were easy to transcribe, and both would have shipped as falsehoods.
Fill this in at the END of Phase 1, from research/sources.md section D
('claims deliberately not made'). Format: {phrase: why it is banned}.
Matching is case-insensitive substring, so write the shortest phrase that is
unambiguously wrong — an affirmative claim, not a word that also appears in
the correction ('syntax highlighting' would ban the sentence that says there
is none; 'syntax-highlighted code blocks are produced' would not).
Prefer banning the AFFIRMATIVE form of the claim.

_template_delete_me.supports nested lists: verified false — indented children render as literal text
_template_delete_me.fully CommonMark compliant: not conformant; entities/escapes/autolinks/indented code all diverge
_template_delete_me.updates are signed: no signature, no pinned commit — SHA-256 is a change detector only
_template_delete_me.PHP 8.3 is enforced: documented, not enforced — there is no version_compare() guard
_template_delete_me.built-in syntax highlighting: no highlighter is loaded anywhere in the repository
_template_delete_me.ships an .htaccess: no .htaccess exists in the repository; any sample is a recommendation

_notes: Also worth banning, once you have verified them absent:
* 'simply' / 'just' before a step that is not simple
* any specific performance number you did not measure
* any version number you did not read from the source
